Proposed change: 'to the skies' -> 'to the heavens'. Here haššāmayim is the destination of a divine taking-up, and the central shamayim entry's own clause scales the rendering toward a numinous register in such contexts. genesis-woh already does this (GEN-WOH-28:12 'reached to the heavens', 19:24, 22:11), and the central human-ascent entry reads 'ascent to heaven'. Line changed from 'as your soul lives' to 'as you yourself live'. ḥay-YHWH wəḥê-napšəḵā is an oath by the addressee's life; nepeš here is the person/life, not a separable soul, so the rendering (cf. NJPS 'as you live') is more exact than ASV. šēḇ-nāʾ p̄ōh; Beit-El. Approved.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ אֵלִיָּ֛הוּ וֶאֱלִישָׁ֖ע מִן־הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when YHWH was about to take Eliyahu up in the whirlwind to the heavens, that Eliyahu and Elisha went from Gilgal.

notes.official:
Names in this chapter: Eliyahu = Elijah, Elisha = Elisha, Beit-El = Bethel, Yericho = Jericho, Yarden = Jordan, Karmel = Carmel, Shomron = Samaria (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

*bassəʿārâ haššāmayim* 'in the whirlwind to the heavens'. *sĕʿārâ* is lexically 'storm, tempest, gale' (HALOT; BDB), and rotation is not part of its meaning. The bare noun keeps the established English 'whirlwind' under the central `min-ha-se-arah` (Job 38:1), while the compound *rûaḥ sĕʿārâ* of Ezek 1:4 is 'a stormy wind' (`ruach-se'arah`). The Hebrew article is kept (ASV 'by a whirlwind'). *haššāmayim* is an accusative of direction, rendered 'to the heavens' (ASV 'into heaven'). Under the central `shamayim` the rendering scales with register: where *šāmayim* names the dwelling of YHWH (1 Kgs 8:30), the corpus uses 'heaven(s)', as genesis-woh does at Gen 22:11 and 28:12; the physical sky of 1 Kgs 18:45 and 2 Kgs 1:10, 12, 14 stays 'skies'. 'Heavens' keeps the plural of the Hebrew.

The verse announces the outcome at the start, so the suspense of the chapter lies in Elisha, not in the event. *bəhaʿălôṯ YHWH* 'when YHWH was about to take ... up' (hiphil of *ʿlh*) makes YHWH the agent. Gilgal, the starting point, is probably a town in the hills near Beit-El, not the Gilgal by the Yarden (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('when Yahweh would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind'; French 'aux cieux dans un tourbillon') as the start of Eliyahu's departure on a craft of the Elohim. The translation renders the Hebrew lexemes by their corpus conventions and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֜ע שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי עַד־בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּרְד֖וּ בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to Elisha, "Please stay here, for YHWH has sent me as far as Beit-El." And Elisha said, "As YHWH lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Beit-El.

notes.official: *ḥay-YHWH wəḥê-napšəḵā* 'As YHWH lives, and as you yourself live' (vv 2, 4, 6): a double oath by YHWH's life and the addressee's (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`). The second member is rendered without ASV 'soul', since *nepeš* here means the person's life (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`; cf. NJPS 'as you live'). Eliyahu tests Elisha three times (Beit-El, Yericho, Yarden), and three times Elisha refuses to leave. Beit-El = Bethel (`bethel-luz-name-etymology`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בֵּֽית־אֵל֮ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הֲיָדַ֕עְתָּ כִּ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם יְהוָ֛ה לֹקֵ֥חַ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ מֵעַ֣ל רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם־אֲנִ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי הֶחֱשֽׁוּ׃

i18n.en: And the sons of the prophets who were at Beit-El came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I too know it; be silent."

notes.official: *bənê-hannəḇîʾîm* 'the sons of the prophets': *bēn* + group noun = 'member of', so these are members of a prophetic community, not prophets' children (`bene-ha-neviim-sons-of-the-prophets-kings`; GKC §128v; NRSV 'company of prophets'). *lōqēaḥ ʾeṯ-ʾăḏōneyḵā mēʿal rōʾšeḵā* 'is taking your master from over your head': *lqḥ* 'take' is the verb of Hanokh's removal in Gen 5:24 (*kî-lāqaḥ ʾōṯô ʾĕlōhîm*; central `veh-einennu-laqach`). These are the Hebrew Bible's two accounts of removal without death. The expression 'over your head' reflects the master's position above a disciple. *heḥĕšû* 'be silent'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע ׀ שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי יְרִיח֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, for YHWH has sent me to Yericho." And he said, "As YHWH lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they came to Yericho.

notes.official: Second test; oath as in v 2 (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`; `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). Yericho = Jericho.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בִּֽירִיחוֹ֮ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הֲיָדַ֕עְתָּ כִּ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם יְהוָ֛ה לֹקֵ֥חַ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ מֵעַ֣ל רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם־אֲנִ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי הֶחֱשֽׁוּ׃

i18n.en: And the sons of the prophets who were at Yericho came near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I too know it; be silent."

notes.official: The prophetic group at Yericho repeats the words of the group at Beit-El (v 3; `bene-ha-neviim-sons-of-the-prophets-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי הַיַּרְדֵּ֔נָה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to him, "Please stay here, for YHWH has sent me to the Yarden." And he said, "As YHWH lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." And the two of them went on.

notes.official: Third test; oath as in v 2 (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`; `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). Yarden = Jordan. *wayyēlḵû šənêhem* 'And the two of them went on': 'the two of them' recurs in vv 7, 8, 11 until the pair is separated.

paragraphs.text: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֨ים אִ֜ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֤י הַנְּבִיאִים֙ הָֽלְכ֔וּ וַיַּעַמְד֥וּ מִנֶּ֖גֶד מֵרָח֑וֹק וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם עָמְד֥וּ עַל־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance; and the two of them stood by the Yarden.

notes.official: The fifty *bənê-hannəḇîʾîm* (`bene-ha-neviim-sons-of-the-prophets-kings`) stand *minneḡeḏ mērāḥôq* 'opposite them at a distance' as witnesses; they see the crossing (v 15) but, unlike Elisha, not the ascent.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ אֶת־אַדַּרְתּ֤וֹ וַיִּגְלֹם֙ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם וַיֵּחָצ֖וּ הֵ֣נָּה וָהֵ֑נָּה וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בֶּחָרָבָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu took his mantle and rolled it up and struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

notes.official: *wayyiqqaḥ ʾēliyyāhû ʾeṯ-ʾaddartô wayyiḡlōm* 'took his mantle and rolled it up': the *ʾadderet* serves as Moses' staff did. The waters divide *hēnnâ wāhēnnâ* 'this way and that' and the two cross *beḥārāḇâ* 'on dry ground', the vocabulary of the sea crossing (Ex 14:21-22) and of the Yarden crossing under Yehoshua (Josh 3:17).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י כְעָבְרָ֗ם וְאֵ֨לִיָּ֜הוּ אָמַ֤ר אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֙ שְׁאַל֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ בְּטֶ֖רֶם אֶלָּקַ֣ח מֵעִמָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע וִֽיהִי־נָ֛א פִּֽי־שְׁנַ֥יִם בְּרוּחֲךָ֖ אֵלָֽי׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when they had crossed over, that Eliyahu said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." And Elisha said, "Please let there be a double portion of your ruach upon me."

notes.official:
*pî-šənayim bərûḥăḵā* 'a double portion of your ruach'. *pî-šənayim* is the firstborn's inheritance share in Deut 21:17 ('a share of two'), and Elisha asks to be Eliyahu's principal heir, not for twice his power (`pi-shenayim-double-portion-2-kings-2-9`; Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*). In Zech 13:8 the same phrase means 'two-thirds'.

*rûaḥ* is transliterated (ASV 'spirit') so that the word Elisha asks for here, the *rûaḥ* seen resting on him in v 15, and the *rûaḥ YHWH* feared in v 16 stay visibly the same (`ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`, inferred). The sense here is the prophet's charismatic endowment, as with Moses' *rûaḥ* shared with the elders (Num 11:17, 25).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִקְשִׁ֣יתָ לִשְׁא֑וֹל אִם־תִּרְאֶ֨ה אֹתִ֜י לֻקָּ֤ח מֵֽאִתָּךְ֙ יְהִֽי־לְךָ֣ כֵ֔ן וְאִם־אַ֖יִן לֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And he said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be."

notes.official: *hiqšîṯā lišʾôl* 'You have asked a hard thing'. The condition, *ʾim-tirʾeh ʾōṯî luqqāḥ mēʾittāḵ* 'If you see me taken from you', makes seeing the event the qualification for succession. Sight is the theme of vv 10-12 and returns at 6:17.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י הֵ֣מָּה הֹלְכִ֤ים הָלוֹךְ֙ וְדַבֵּ֔ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה רֶֽכֶב־אֵשׁ֙ וְס֣וּסֵי אֵ֔שׁ וַיַּפְרִ֖דוּ בֵּ֣ין שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּ֙עַל֙ אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as they were still going on and talking, that behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and they separated the two of them; and Eliyahu went up in the whirlwind to the heavens.

notes.official:
*wəhinnēh rekeḇ-ʾēš wəsûsê ʾēš wayyaprîḏû bên šənêhem* 'behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and they separated the two of them': a verbless presentative clause and a plural verb. The ASV's supplied 'there appeared' is not added, and the plural verb is made explicit (ASV 'which parted them both asunder'). The construct chains are kept literal (`rekhev-esh-susei-esh-chariot-and-horses-of-fire-2-kings-2-11`). *rekeḇ* can be a single chariot or collective 'chariotry'. Fiery chariots and horses form the heavenly army around Elisha at 6:17, and divine chariots belong to storm-theophany imagery (Ps 68:18; 104:3; Hab 3:8).

*wayyaʿal ʾēliyyāhû bassəʿārâ haššāmāyim* 'and Eliyahu went up in the whirlwind to the heavens': the storm, not the chariot, is the vehicle of the ascent in the Hebrew. *sĕʿārâ* per `min-ha-se-arah` ('whirlwind'; lexically 'storm', see v 1); *šāmayim* 'the heavens' per `shamayim` (see v 1). The Mesopotamian and Hebrew ascent traditions (Adapa, Etana, Hanokh) are collected in the central `human-ascent-to-heaven-adapa-etana-enoch-elijah-cross-corpus`, cited here as comparative background.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** This is the central Kings citation of The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3), which reads the chariot and horses of fire as an eyewitness's description of a flying craft taking off, its exhaust flames seen as horses of fire. That reading is the canon's interpretation of the event. The translation renders the Hebrew literally ('chariot of fire', 'horses of fire', 'whirlwind', 'heavens') and uses no technical vocabulary.

paragraphs.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֣ע רֹאֶ֗ה וְה֤וּא מְצַעֵק֙ אָבִ֣י ׀ אָבִ֗י רֶ֤כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפָ֣רָשָׁ֔יו וְלֹ֥א רָאָ֖הוּ ע֑וֹד וַֽיַּחֲזֵק֙ בִּבְגָדָ֔יו וַיִּקְרָעֵ֖ם לִשְׁנַ֥יִם קְרָעִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Elisha was seeing it, and he was crying out, "My father, my father, the chariots of Yisra'el and its horsemen!" And he saw him no more. And he took hold of his own garments and tore them in two pieces.

notes.official: *ʾāḇî ʾāḇî rekeḇ yiśrāʾēl ûp̄ārāšāyw* 'My father, my father, the chariots of Yisra'el and its horsemen!': the doubled vocative (`doubled-name-call-theophanic-formula`) and a fixed epithet. The same cry is uttered over Elisha at his death (2 Kgs 13:14), and it names the prophet as Israel's true military strength (`rekhev-esh-susei-esh-chariot-and-horses-of-fire-2-kings-2-11`). *rekeḇ* is the same singular form as in v 11. ASV 'a chariot' there and 'the chariots' here reflects its collective range, and the ASV is kept. *pārāšîm* may be 'horsemen' (ASV) or 'horses, steeds' (HALOT *pārāš*). 'My father' is the address of a disciple to a master, and it fits the inheritance language of v 9. Tearing the garments *lišnayim qərāʿîm* 'in two pieces' is a mourning rite.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֙רֶם֙ אֶת־אַדֶּ֣רֶת אֵלִיָּ֔הוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָפְלָ֖ה מֵעָלָ֑יו וַיָּ֥שָׁב וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And he picked up the mantle of Eliyahu that had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Yarden.

notes.official: The *ʾadderet* 'that had fallen from him' passes to Elisha: the mantle cast on him at 1 Kgs 19:19 is now his.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֶת־אַדֶּ֨רֶת אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֲשֶׁר־נָפְלָ֤ה מֵֽעָלָיו֙ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אַיֵּ֕ה יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ אַף־ה֣וּא ׀ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֗יִם וַיֵּֽחָצוּ֙ הֵ֣נָּה וָהֵ֔נָּה וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

i18n.en: And he took the mantle of Eliyahu that had fallen from him and struck the waters and said, "Where is YHWH, the Elohim of Eliyahu?" And when he too had struck the waters, they were divided this way and that; and Elisha crossed over.

notes.official: *ʾayyēh YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾēliyyāhû ʾap̄-hûʾ*: the major disjunctive accent of the verse falls on *ʾēliyyāhû*, so the Masoretic division closes the question there and makes *ʾap̄-hûʾ* 'he too, even he' open the second half: 'And when he too had struck the waters'. The ASV takes it the same way, and the translation follows the accents. The LXX transliterates *aphphō*, which some take as *ʾēp̄ôʾ* 'where is he now?' and attach to the question (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`; Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*, ad loc.). Elisha repeats Eliyahu's act of v 8, and the waters divide again: the succession is confirmed.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְאֻ֨הוּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־בִּֽירִיחוֹ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נָ֛חָה ר֥וּחַ אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ עַל־אֱלִישָׁ֑ע וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֖וֹ אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And when the sons of the prophets who were at Yericho saw him from opposite, they said, "The ruach of Eliyahu rests on Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.

notes.official: *nāḥâ rûaḥ ʾēliyyāhû ʿal-ʾĕlîšāʿ* 'The ruach of Eliyahu rests on Elisha': the endowment requested in v 9, now recognized by the prophetic group (`ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`; `bene-ha-neviim-sons-of-the-prophets-kings`; cf. Num 11:25-26, *wayyānaḥ ʿălêhem hārûaḥ*). Their bowing to the ground acknowledges Elisha as the new master.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֡יו הִנֵּה־נָ֣א יֵֽשׁ־אֶת־עֲבָדֶיךָ֩ חֲמִשִּׁ֨ים אֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּנֵֽי־חַ֗יִל יֵ֣לְכוּ נָא֮ וִיבַקְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶיךָ֒ פֶּן־נְשָׂאוֹ֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלִכֵ֙הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הֶהָרִ֔ים א֖וֹ בְּאַחַ֣ת הגיאות [הַגֵּאָי֑וֹת] וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֥א תִשְׁלָֽחוּ׃

i18n.en: And they said to him, "Behold now, there are with your servants fifty strong men; please let them go and seek your master, lest the ruach of YHWH has taken him up and cast him on one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." And he said, "You shall not send."

notes.official:
*pen-nəśāʾô rûaḥ YHWH wayyašlīḵēhû* 'lest the ruach of YHWH has taken him up and cast him': the same fear Ovadyahu voiced at 1 Kgs 18:12 (`ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`). Coming right after the ascent in the storm (v 11), the phrase can be heard as 'wind of YHWH', and the transliteration keeps both senses open. The prophets assume that Eliyahu has been displaced, not removed. The fruitless search (v 17) confirms the narrator's account for them.

Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *hgyʾwt* / Qere *haggēʾāyôṯ* 'the valleys', an orthographic variant with the same sense; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפְצְרוּ־ב֥וֹ עַד־בֹּ֖שׁ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלָ֑חוּ וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ וַיְבַקְשׁ֥וּ שְׁלֹשָֽׁה־יָמִ֖ים וְלֹ֥א מְצָאֻֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And when they urged him until he was ashamed, he said, "Send." So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.

notes.official: *ʿaḏ-bōš* 'until he was ashamed': until Elisha was too embarrassed to refuse any longer (cf. 8:11). The three-day search mirrors the three tests of vv 2-6.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ אֵלָ֔יו וְה֖וּא יֹשֵׁ֣ב בִּירִיח֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם הֲלֽוֹא־אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אַל־תֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

i18n.en: And they came back to him while he was staying at Yericho; and he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֔ע הִנֵּה־נָ֞א מוֹשַׁ֤ב הָעִיר֙ ט֔וֹב כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י רֹאֶ֑ה וְהַמַּ֥יִם רָעִ֖ים וְהָאָ֥רֶץ מְשַׁכָּֽלֶת׃

i18n.en: And the men of the city said to Elisha, "Behold now, the situation of the city is good, as my lord sees; but the water is bad, and the land miscarries."

notes.official: *wəhāʾāreṣ məšakkāleṯ* 'and the land miscarries': piel participle of *škl* 'be bereaved, miscarry'. The water causes miscarriage in people or livestock, or the land fails to bear. ASV 'the land miscarrieth' is kept. Yericho's spring is traditionally identified with ʿEin es-Sulṭan.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קְחוּ־לִי֙ צְלֹחִ֣ית חֲדָשָׁ֔ה וְשִׂ֥ימוּ שָׁ֖ם מֶ֑לַח וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֵלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it." And they brought it to him.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ אֶל־מוֹצָ֣א הַמַּ֔יִם וַיַּשְׁלֶךְ־שָׁ֖ם מֶ֑לַח וַיֹּ֜אמֶר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רִפִּ֙אתִי֙ לַמַּ֣יִם הָאֵ֔לֶּה לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה מִשָּׁ֛ם ע֖וֹד מָ֥וֶת וּמְשַׁכָּֽלֶת׃

i18n.en: And he went out to the spring of the waters and threw salt there and said, "Thus says YHWH: 'I have healed these waters; from there there shall be no more death or miscarrying.'"

notes.official: *rippīṯî lammayim hāʾēlleh* 'I have healed these waters': the prophetic messenger formula 'Thus says YHWH' credits the healing to YHWH. The scene recalls Moses sweetening the waters of Marah (Ex 15:23-25, where YHWH is 'your healer'). *ûməšakkāleṯ* 'or miscarrying', as in v 19.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּרָפ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּדְבַ֥ר אֱלִישָׁ֖ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So the waters were healed unto this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.

notes.official: *ʿaḏ hayyôm hazzeh* 'unto this day' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`): the editorial note that the spring remained sweet in the narrator's time.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְה֣וּא ׀ עֹלֶ֣ה בַדֶּ֗רֶךְ וּנְעָרִ֤ים קְטַנִּים֙ יָצְא֣וּ מִן־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּתְקַלְּסוּ־בוֹ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ עֲלֵ֥ה קֵרֵ֖חַ עֲלֵ֥ה קֵרֵֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And he went up from there to Beit-El; and as he was going up by the way, young lads came out of the city and jeered at him and said to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"

notes.official: *nəʿārîm qəṭannîm* 'young lads' (v 24 *yəlāḏîm* 'children'): *naʿar* covers anyone from a child to a young man or servant (cf. 1 Kgs 3:7, where Solomon, a king, calls himself *naʿar qāṭōn*), so the age of the mockers cannot be fixed. The ASV-based wording is kept. *ʿălēh qērēaḥ* 'Go up, baldhead!': 'go up' may mock the report of Eliyahu's ascent ('go up as your master did'), and the baldness may be natural or a tonsure marking a prophet (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*). Beit-El, the royal shrine of the northern kingdom (1 Kgs 12:29), is the setting (`bethel-luz-name-etymology`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן אַֽחֲרָיו֙ וַיִּרְאֵ֔ם וַֽיְקַלְלֵ֖ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה שְׁתַּ֤יִם דֻּבִּים֙ מִן־הַיַּ֔עַר וַתְּבַקַּ֣עְנָה מֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁנֵ֖י יְלָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he turned behind him and saw them, and cursed them in the name of YHWH. And two she-bears came out of the forest and tore forty-two children of them.

notes.official: *wayqalləlēm bəšēm YHWH* 'and cursed them in the name of YHWH'. The punishment answers contempt for YHWH's prophet, a theme of the chapter's two 'up/down' narratives (cf. 1:9-12). *šətayim dubbîm* 'two she-bears' and 'forty-two' (cf. 10:14) are typical narrative numbers. The episode is a legitimation story for Elisha (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל־הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he went from there to Mount Karmel, and from there he returned to Shomron.

notes.official: Elisha's route returns him to Karmel (the scene of 1 Kgs 18) and to Shomron (Samaria), the capital, setting up the Elisha cycle of 2 Kgs 3-8.
